analysis.title: The Most Hated Trades Are Suddenly Getting Interesting
key_insights: SOX bounced off its 200-day moving average and the lower end of the range in place since May. The range remains intact, and chasing breakouts in either direction has been costly.

Goldman says Korea's electronics sector accounted for roughly 60% of the country's annual GDP growth in Q3. Tech exports remain strong, machinery investment accelerated and semiconductor equipment imports kept rising, despite a sharp valuation reset in semiconductor equities.

BofA says SMH offers one of the most attractive upside call-spread payouts among liquid ETFs that have sold off since the October 6 Nasdaq peak. December at-the-money call spreads targeting a one-standard-deviation rebound offered roughly 2.8x payout as of October 26.
Goldman says CTAs sold nearly $3bn of Nasdaq 100 futures over the past three sessions, the largest three-day selling wave since March 2025.

Deutsche Bank says October 27 has historically marked the final seasonal low for the S&P 500, with equities typically rallying into year-end. The S&P 500 rose over the three months following early October in 21 of the past 23 midterm years.
JPM says the CAC 40 trades at its cheapest relative valuation to the Eurozone on record, after more than three years of underperformance and with deeply negative sentiment.
Goldman says GLD recorded its biggest weekly outflow since March after the recent gold washout.
Goldman says CTAs are running sizable gold shorts. The last time positioning was this bearish was just before the August short squeeze.
Silver trades 25% below its 200-day moving average, the widest discount since the March 2020 liquidation. The last comparable dislocation was in 2013.
TS Lombard says Brazil's debt-to-GDP ratio has risen to 81.9% from 71.7% when Lula took office in 2023. Under a business-as-usual scenario, debt reaches almost 118% of GDP by 2036.

TS Lombard warns that without fiscal reform Brazil could face a partial government shutdown in 2028, as mandatory spending crowds out discretionary spending below the level needed to operate the government.

sector_views.rationale: SOX holds its 200-day average and range support. Korean activity data show strong tech exports and semiconductor equipment imports, which question whether the sell-off went too far.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 71.7% in 2023. TS Lombard projects almost 118% by 2036 under business-as-usual.
Business-as-usual scenario implies an unsustainable fiscal path without reform.
